raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been working these fields for 45 years, and this little 2-mu plot isn't going to make me rich — at my age it's more about keeping busy and keeping some grain and cash coming in for me and the old lady. Just the two of us at home now. But I've had schooling, I read the extension pamphlets when they come around, and I still pay attention to what the agricultural station is saying about rates and timing.

**Crop choice.** I'm sticking with spring maize (春玉米) — it's what fits this plot given I'm not doing the wheat-maize double rotation. Spring maize has a longer season, yields better per mu than summer maize if you manage it right, and I'm not rushing to clear wheat off in June. At my age, the relaxed calendar matters.

**Variety and planting.** I'll buy Zhengdan 958 (郑单958) seed again — solid variety, handles our conditions, I know how it behaves at every stage. Some of the younger guys are trying Denghai or Xianyu 335, but I'd rather stick with what I know yields reliably here. Plant around late April, after soil temp gets steady above 10°C at 10 cm depth. Density around 4,500 plants per mu — that's what the station recommends for this variety and what experience tells me works on my soil.

**Fertilizer.** With my education I actually think about this rather than just dumping. For a 500 kg/mu yield target, I'm planning about 17 kg N per mu total, split: base application of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at ~40 kg/mu before planting, giving me 6 kg each of N, P₂O₅, K₂O as base. Then topdress urea at jointing (V6-V8 stage), another 24 kg urea/mu which is about 11 kg N. That gets me 17 kg N, 6 P, 6 K per mu. A university type would split the N three ways but for spring maize on 2 mu, two applications is good enough — the extra labor trip isn't worth it for me.

**Irrigation.** I've got the well, which is a blessing. I'll plan on 2 irrigations: one at jointing if there's no decent rain in June, and the critical one at tasseling/silking in late July — that's the one you never skip on spring maize, yield loss is too big if the crop stresses then. If a drought really sets in I might do a third, but pumping costs money so I'd rather not.

**Weeds and pests.** Pre-emergence herbicide right after planting — acetochlor plus atrazine, standard stuff, about 25 yuan/mu. Saves me bending over to weed, which at 68 I appreciate. I'll watch for fall armyworm (草地贪夜蛾) — it's been a problem recent years — and spray insecticide only if I see damage, not preventively.

**Tillage.** I don't own a tractor for just 2 mu, so I hire the village guy to do rotary tillage before planting. About 40 yuan/mu. He plants with the small machine too when he comes through.

**Labor.** Just me and my wife. She helps at planting and harvest. For 2 mu across the whole season, maybe 12-15 family-days total — it's not much work at this scale. No hired labor needed.

**Yield expectation.** I'm targeting 500 kg/mu. Got 520 last year, but I don't want to count on that. With the irrigation access and my experience, 500 is realistic; anything above is a good year.
